_comment: Genuinely known points — the only real ground truth in this exercise.
Copy this file to truth.json and fill it in. truth.json is GITIGNORED and
must stay that way: these are people's home rooftops, which is personal
data and does not belong in a repository.
FORMAT. One object per point. Four required fields, all flat:
lat   number, decimal degrees, north positive. 5+ decimal places.
lng   number, decimal degrees, east positive. NOT nested, NOT a string.
city  must match a city in PAKISTAN_LOCATIONS exactly, e.g. "Karachi".
area  the area YOU know the point to be in. It must resolve against the
registry — calibrate.js validates every one of these BEFORE
spending a single API call and tells you which ones failed.
Spelling is forgiving: aliases and the Town/Sector affix rules
apply, so "Landhi Town" and "Landhi" both work.
Anything without a numeric lat is skipped, which is why this comment
object is harmless. Add "note" or any other field freely; it is ignored.
HOW TO PICK POINTS, cheapest first:
1. Team members' own addresses — a pin on their own roof plus the area
name. Twenty of these beat two hundred unlabelled records.
2. Unambiguous landmarks — hospitals, universities, markets whose area
is not in dispute.
3. Points deliberately NEAR area boundaries. That is where geocoders
fail and where the containment threshold gets tuned; sampling only
comfortable interiors over-reports accuracy. Aim for about a third.
These points do NOT need to appear in any sweep. calibrate.js geocodes
them directly:
set -a; source .env.geocode; set +a
node scripts/geocode-spike/calibrate.js
Cost is one Google and one LocationIQ call per point — 25 points is a few
cents. Getting the coordinate right matters far more than getting many.

note: optional; ignored by the scorer. Use it to record boundary points.
